threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused when the bus route changes mid-journey. Everyone else is just rolling with it like it's part of the experience.
Last night on the 47, the driver stopped for a cat crossing the road. Gave it a nod like they were old mates. Only in Bermondsey.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I found an old lady selling homemade jams under the S-Bahn bridge, chatting with regulars like it was the local pub.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You know you're in Kreuzberg when you see a group of guys playing chess on a traffic island. It's the unofficial sport of the block.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they know which BART delays mean they have to take the long walk to 16th instead of waiting for a train.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: The 31 Balboa had a guy trying to sell his mixtape—while we all crammed in like sardines. Only in SF do the morning commutes come with a soundtrack.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all locals love the Sagrada Família. Many of us avoid it—too many crowds and overpriced cafés nearby. Hidden gems are everywhere!

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They stand at the market prices, baffled by how cheap the fruit is, then treat themselves to overpriced avocado toast at a nearby café.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You know they’re new when they don’t yet know the best spots for a late-night kebab after a gig—everyone's got a favorite, it’s a rite of passage.
Caught a guy in a tweed coat ordering a kebab while pretending to conduct an orchestra. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I was home when the bakery on Sonnenallee started saving me a piece of my favorite cake every Friday. It felt like family.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find a 24/7 Döner that’s packed at 3 AM with locals debating the best street art. It's a rite of passage.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a true local when they can name the exact time the BART delays kick in during rush hour, and it’s not just the usual 5 o’clock traffic.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Spotted a guy playing sax on the 49 going over the bridge, traffic stopped. He turned it into a serenade for the passengers—crowd loved it.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think we all love the Festa Major de Gràcia, but many locals just want to avoid the crowds and get back to our usual life.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their hesitation at the Pl. del Sol roundabout, staring confusedly at the bike lanes while holding a map.
